# v0.10.0 — One service, one account of the plug-in

Stable release of the 0.10 series, compared with the last stable version 0.9.1.

- **One service for every connection:** a direct USB or LAN connection runs the same service as the app. Guest charging, departure planning and all targets work the same everywhere.
- **Cost target:** charge for an amount of money in Home Assistant's currency. The service books the energy at each reported price, keeps the money used through restarts and stops the charge itself. A reached energy or cost target ends with the unplug.
- **Safer on the line:** after a lost answer the RTU line falls silent before the next request, so a late answer is never mistaken for the next one, and every start, restart or release is judged after that wait. Waiting pauses, locks and withdrawn releases are no longer lost to a missing reply, a failed poll or another command.
- **One account of the plug-in** decides for Plug & Charge, guest charging, the unplug rule and the charging estimates whether a car is connected. Losses and costs are measured by the service over the car's own plug cycle, also through Home Assistant restarts.
- **Clearer interface:** one Charging status, one Charging wait reason and one Activity event; the same target names in Home Assistant and the app; the app sorts its targets by whom they apply to. The departure blueprints act only for their own car, never for a guest.

**Updating from 0.9.1:** update the app and the integration to **0.10.0** together (service API 3).

- Confirm the safe reset under **Settings → System → Repairs**, then set your targets again.
- Removed sensors, event entities and buttons have replacements (see the changelog); update automations on the new Activity event types.
- Departure planning is now `departure_*`: set your vehicles up again, and delete the old, unavailable Target time entity before the new one appears.
- Switch off charging release when unplugged is now an integration option, off by default.
- A standalone service container runs as UID 10001 and needs a writable data directory.

Hardware tests on the maintainer's wallbox look good so far; please report what you see on other wallboxes.

Every contribution is voluntary and very welcome; support and new features stay open to everyone either way.
